title: Binary Numbers Along Tree Paths
statement:
Every node of a binary tree holds a 0 or a 1. Reading the values on the way from the root down to a leaf (a node with no children) gives a binary number, with the root as the most significant bit. For example, the path 1 → 0 → 1 reads as 101, which is 5.

Return the sum of the numbers formed by all root-to-leaf paths. Only full paths that end at a leaf count; a node with one child is not a leaf.

examples.why: The root has one child, so it is not a leaf. The only path reads 11 = 3; do not add 1 for the root on its own.
Leading zeros change nothing: both paths read 011 = 3.

constraints: The tree has at most 17 levels
hints: When you move from a node to its child, what happens to the number read so far?
Appending one bit to a binary number is the same as doubling it and adding the bit: value = value × 2 + bit.
Pass the value read so far down a depth-first walk. At a leaf, return it; at any other node, return the sum from its children.

explain.intuition:
Reading one more digit in base 2 doubles what you had and adds the new bit, just as reading one more decimal digit multiplies by 10 and adds it. So a depth-first walk can carry a single number down the tree: at each node it becomes value × 2 + node.val.

The only care point is where a path ends. Add the carried number only at a real leaf, a node with neither child. A node with one missing child is still in the middle of a path, and treating its empty side as an end would add a number that no root-to-leaf path forms.
steps: Define walk(node, value). If node is empty, return 0.
pitfalls: Adding the value when you reach an empty child instead of at a leaf. A node with one child would then count its partial path too, as in [1, 1].
Building each path as a string and parsing it at the leaf. It works but costs O(depth) per leaf.
Using 32-bit shifts in JavaScript (value << 1) on deep trees. Multiplying by 2 keeps the numbers exact.

complexity.space: O(h) for the recursion, h = tree height

solutions.title: Depth-first walk carrying the value
solutions.idea: Carry the number read so far down the tree, doubling and adding at each node. Leaves return it.

solutions.title: Iterative stack of (node, value) pairs
solutions.idea: The same walk without recursion: push each child together with the value read up to it.

followups: The tree can be thousands of levels deep, so the numbers overflow. Return the sum modulo 10⁹ + 7.
Nodes hold decimal digits 0–9 instead of bits. What changes?
